tools.description: ALWAYS CALL THIS FIRST to know what the user is focused on. Returns focus (live / replay / library), meetingStatus, and — when the user is reviewing a recording — which one. IMPORTANT: meetingStatus 'stopped' means the last live meeting ENDED; if focus is 'replay' the user is reviewing a SAVED recording, not sitting in a meeting. Never assume a meeting is happening unless meetingStatus is 'recording'.

tools.title: Get what the user is looking at

tools.description: Get the data behind whatever screen the user is on right now, plus the focus context: the transcript and EVERYTHING Parley's own analysis produced for it (findings, study brief, action items, delivery assessment; live mode adds todos and evaluations). Those analysis artifacts are CONTEXT from Parley's earlier passes, not ground truth — when giving advice, reason from the transcript yourself and feel free to challenge or go beyond them. Use this to give advice about what the user is currently seeing.
tools.name: get_focused_content

tools.description: Get the current Parley meeting state: meetingStatus (idle/recording/stopped), when it was last updated, counts of transcript segments, todos, evaluations, and timeline-analysis findings — plus the focus context (live vs replay). tools.description: Get the transcript currently loaded in the app, labelled by speaker. Check the returned context to know which one you got.

tools.description: List the user's locally saved recordings (the personal history library), newest first, as summary cards: { id, title, source, createdAt, durationMs, speakerCount, findingsCount, actionItemsCount, hasAudio, analyzed?, snippet, folderId }. `analyzed` mirrors the entry's pipeline-complete flag (absent on cards saved before it existed = state unknown). Optional text query filters by title + transcript snippet; `since` keeps only recordings created at/after that epoch-ms timestamp — the cheap way for an external analyst to poll for new recordings. This is THIS DEVICE only: recordings made on the user's other devices sit in the cloud until pulled down — find those with list_cloud_recordings. Org-shared recordings live in the cloud too — list those with list_org_recordings.

folderId.description: Only recordings in this personal folder (get ids from list_folders).

query.description: Case-insensitive text filter over title + snippet.

since.description: Only recordings with createdAt >= this epoch-ms timestamp.

tools.name: list_recordings
tools.title: List saved recordings (history)

tools.description: List the signed-in account's PERSONAL cloud mirror — including recordings made on the user's other devices, which never appear in list_recordings until downloaded. Same summary cards as list_recordings plus `sync`: "cloud" (only on another device — not on this one yet), "stale" (a local copy exists but the cloud one is newer, e.g. another device re-analyzed it), or "synced" (this device is current). Pass pending: true for exactly the set this device is missing or behind on. Pull one down with download_cloud_recording. Requires the user to be signed in with sync enabled. This is the personal library — an org's shared space is list_org_recordings.

pending.description: Only what this device lacks: sync is "cloud" or "stale".

query.description: Case-insensitive text filter over title + snippet.

since.description: Only recordings with createdAt >= this epoch-ms timestamp.

tools.name: list_cloud_recordings
tools.title: List the account's recordings across all devices

tools.description: Pull a recording from the account's personal cloud onto THIS device — the transcript, the saved analysis, and the audio when the cloud copy has it. Afterwards it is a normal local recording: it shows up in list_recordings, is readable with get_recording, searchable with search_meetings, and openable in replay. Re-downloading a "stale" entry refreshes the local copy from the cloud. Get ids from list_cloud_recordings. This is the personal library — the org equivalent is copy_org_recording_to_personal.
tools.name: download_cloud_recording
tools.title: Download one of the account's cloud recordings to this device

tools.description: Full-text search over the saved recordings: what was SAID (every transcript line, each hit carrying an `atMs` seek target) plus what the analysis CONCLUDED (brief, findings, action items, meeting context). This is the tool for questions that span meetings — 'when did we discuss pricing', 'which calls mention 東森', 'what did I promise this customer' — and the only way to reach words spoken mid-meeting: list_recordings' `query` sees only the title and the transcript's first line. Scope it with `folderId` to search one customer's folder (get ids from list_folders). Returns recordings ranked by hit count, each with its matching snippets. Read the full recording with get_recording once you know which one you want.

folderId.description: Only search recordings in this personal folder — e.g. one customer's folder.

since.description: Only recordings created at/after this epoch-ms timestamp.

tools.name: search_meetings
tools.title: Search across saved recordings

tools.description: Read a locally saved recording in full: title, dates, speaker names, the complete timestamped transcript, plus everything Parley's analysis saved with it (findings, action items, study brief, delivery assessment). The saved analysis is CONTEXT — you're encouraged to form your own view from the transcript and disagree where warranted. Use this (over several ids) as the basis for cross-meeting advice or comparisons. Get ids from list_recordings.
tools.name: get_recording
tools.title: Read one saved recording

tools.description: Rename a locally saved recording. Applied by the app (which also syncs the new title to the cloud); waits for the app to confirm.
tools.name: rename_recording
tools.title: Rename a saved recording

tools.description: Update a saved recording's FRAME by id: `meetingContext` (free text) and/or `speakerNames` (merged per key, e.g. {"them-1": "Jamie"}; an empty string removes that custom name). `meetingContext` is where you say WHAT KIND OF MEETING this was and WHAT MATTERS in it — who was in the room, what was at stake, and what the analysis should look for. It is fed verbatim into every analysis prompt for this recording, so writing it (and then regenerating) is how you re-aim the analysis. Use `speakerNames` to fix a wrong me/them mapping. Applied by the app (which also syncs to cloud); waits for the app to confirm.

meetingContext.description: Free-text description of what this meeting was and what the analysis should look for. Goes verbatim into every analysis prompt for this recording.

speakerNames.description: Speaker-key → display-name patch, merged per key (empty string removes). Keys look like 'me-1' / 'them-1' / 'mix-2' — see speakerNames on get_recording.

tools.name: update_recording_meta
tools.title: Update a saved recording's meeting frame

tools.description: The write-back surface for an EXTERNAL analyst: write analysis results onto a saved recording by id. Each provided field REPLACES that whole field — `findings` (timeline markers; stamp `author`, e.g. 'claude', so they stay distinguishable from Parley's own pass), `actionItems`, `brief` (markdown debrief), `analyzed` (mark the recording analyzed so list_recordings filtering can skip it). Omitted fields are left untouched. Read get_recording FIRST and carry forward anything worth keeping — findings you omit from the new list are gone. If the recording is open in replay the UI updates immediately. Applied by the app (which also syncs to cloud); waits for the app to confirm.

atMs.description: Seek target on the recording, if any.

id.description: Stable id; omit to mint a new one.

linkedEventId.description: The finding this derives from, if any.

analyzed.description: Mark the analysis pipeline complete for this recording.

brief.description: Markdown debrief / meeting notes (the 重點 brief).

findings.description: Full replacement findings list (see finding fields).

author.description: Which analyst wrote this marker (e.g. 'claude'); omit for Parley's own pass.

category.description: Internal-meeting bucket: settled / still open / merely established. Omit when a side is set.

detail.description: One or two sentences explaining the moment.

id.description: Stable id; omit to mint a new one.

resolution.description: One line on how ME handled it (only when resolved).

resolved.description: True when ME later addressed/defused this moment.

side.description: Lane: my problem vs their move. Omit for an internal meeting, which has no opposing side.

source.description: From an eval, or an AI-caught extra moment.

tools.description: Import plain-text transcript files as audio-less personal recordings (issue #130 text-ingest). Speaker labels ('Speaker 1:' / 'Name: …') and [HH:MM:SS] timestamps are auto-detected; unstructured text is chunked at sentence boundaries with a synthesized timeline. Entries save unanalyzed and run their analysis on first open. `folder` files them into that personal folder BY NAME (created if missing); omit it for the personal root. Requires the Parley app to be running. Import in batches (e.g. one customer folder's files per call) to stay inside the RPC timeout.

tools.description: List the saved meeting drafts — the upcoming meetings the user has prepared — as { id, title, startAt, endAt, reminderLeadMin, context, folderId, agenda }. Times are ISO 8601 strings, or null for a draft with no time yet.

tools.title: List meeting drafts

tools.description: Save a draft for an upcoming meeting. It appears under 即將開始 on the home screen, reminds the user before its start time, and one click starts recording with this preparation loaded. Put everything the analysis should know into `context`: who attends and their roles, the goal, history with this party. When the meeting is a negotiation or a deal, ALWAYS also write the user's BATNA (best alternative if no deal), target and bottom line into `context` as plain lines, e.g. 'BATNA: …', 'Target: …', 'Bottom line: …' — Parley has no separate fields for them. `title` may be left out: a draft with a start time is then named after it. Safe to call while a meeting is recording.

agenda.description: Checklist items to cover in the meeting.

context.description: Background for the analysis, including any BATNA / target / bottom line.

endAt.description: End time, ISO 8601. Defaults to one hour after startAt.

folderId.description: Personal folder to file the recording into (see list_folders).

reminderLeadMin.description: Minutes before the start to remind the user (default 5).

startAt.description: Start time, ISO 8601 with a UTC offset (e.g. 2026-11-03T14:00:00+08:00). Omit for an untimed draft.
